appsIntro.content: The principles of recursive analysis appear across many computing contexts. Their relevance in each domain depends on the exact problem and implementation.

tradeoff.content: Algorithm design is a trade-off between correctness, efficiency, simplicity and resource constraints: a method excellent under one input model may be unsuitable under another.

rows.question: Where can these concepts be applied?
rows.answer: Wherever problems decompose into smaller instances of themselves: data organisation, searching, scheduling, graph processing, text processing, databases, compilers, operating systems, networking and scientific computing.

rows.question: What are the limitations of your research?
rows.answer: It is theoretical, so asymptotic bounds do not capture hardware, compiler or cache effects, and no empirical measurements were performed. Results also depend on input assumptions.

rows.name: Data Organization
rows.detail: Recursive decomposition supports hierarchical ways of structuring and maintaining data.

rows.name: Searching
rows.detail: Repeatedly reducing the search space is naturally expressed and analysed recursively.

rows.name: Scheduling
rows.detail: Complex tasks can be represented as smaller subproblems and analysed by decomposition.

rows.name: Graph Processing
rows.detail: Recursive traversal applies where structures are hierarchical or connected.

rows.name: Text Processing
rows.detail: Recursive structure supports parsing and pattern-oriented processing of input.

rows.name: Database Operations
rows.detail: Relevant to hierarchical data and recursive query evaluation.

rows.name: Compilers
rows.detail: Syntax analysis and parsing are classically recursive in structure.

rows.name: Operating Systems
rows.detail: Recursive traversal suits hierarchical structures such as file systems.

rows.name: Networking
rows.detail: Applies to routing and hierarchical packet-processing problems.

rows.name: Scientific Computing
rows.detail: Recursive mathematical structures help model and simulate complex processes.

rows.name: Systematic
rows.detail: Provides a structured solution to a clearly defined computational problem.

rows.name: Measurable
rows.detail: Allows efficiency to be evaluated using standard asymptotic measures.

rows.name: Implementable
rows.detail: Can usually be realised with well-understood data structures.

rows.name: Foundational
rows.detail: Provides a basis for more advanced algorithmic techniques.

rows.name: Theory is not exact runtime
rows.detail: Complexity does not capture every hardware, compiler or cache effect.

rows.name: Input assumptions matter
rows.detail: Some methods depend strongly on data distribution or representation.

rows.name: Memory cost of speed
rows.detail: Better performance may demand additional memory or implementation complexity.

rows.name: Fit before choice
rows.detail: Selecting an algorithm requires matching its assumptions to the actual problem.
